narrative.title: Slotting a Checkpoint into the Two-Way Corridor
narrative.scenario: A facility adds a new checkpoint to a two-way corridor. The placement rule is relative: the checkpoint must slot in immediately after the p-th one (0-based). Because the corridor is two-way, the crew must wire four links — the newcomer's forward and backward registers, plus updated registers on both of its new neighbours — or patrols will deadlock.
narrative.inputFormat: An array arr of node values, a 0-based position p, and an integer x.
narrative.outputFormat: The list after inserting x immediately after the p-th node.

testCases.explanation: Position 2 is the tail, so the newcomer becomes the new tail with only a backward link to wire.
Inserting after the head rewires both the head's forward link and the old second node's backward link.

hintLevels: Level 1: The newcomer always lands between two existing nodes — right after position p — never before the head.
Level 2: Walk to the p-th node, then splice: newcomer.prev = node, newcomer.next = node.next, node.next = newcomer.
Level 3: The fourth link is the one that breaks lists — when the newcomer is not the new tail, its next node's prev must be updated; skip that and backwards traversal diverges.
